null_model.name: per-dimension configuration model
null_model.preserves: each work's own number of values on that dimension, and the dimension's per-value prevalence
null_model.does_not_preserve: correlations between values inside a work, so the excess here is an upper bound on any structure attributed to a dimension whose detector fires on co-occurring strings
null_model.why_not_a_permutation: the mean over a complete graph is invariant to permuting which work owns which set, so a label-shuffled control would return the observed number and call it a null

pair_graph.why_a_second_population: the model comparison refuses a pair below the declared minimum comparable keys, so the means it pools are measured over 1237 of 2080 pairs covering 52 of 65 works, and a work rich enough to be scored is not a random work. On this corpus the observed mean of `D4_cosmic_function`, read as `declared_rule`, moves 0.098787 between the carrier graph and the scored graph — further than the 0.05 this scan uses to call an excess indistinguishable from chance. So a chance line has to name the graph it was drawn on before anyone subtracts it, and the chance numbers below come from the scored graph alone. This is the population the M4 block-profile test reads.

sensitivity_under_the_endorsement_frame.why: a block ordering that flips between the candidate frame and the endorsement frame is not a fact about the traditions; the two frames differ only in how loudly the detector fired

pairs.reading: a high pair is a candidate for a shared transmission route, not evidence of one; and the inverted list is the shape M4 says should be rare, so it is the list a reviewer should read first

what_this_is_not: no dates, so no transmission claim; detector output over English translations, not human coding; works are not independent, so dependence is flagged per pair rather than filtered away; the chance line comes from the corpus's own marginals
